title: Tail-aware SLI normalization, model prioritization, and failover guardrails
creator: Evelyn Cho
description: Purpose: Define per-endpoint and per-model SLIs with a tail-aware normalization method, a priority-driven error-budget allocation, and deterministic circuit-breaker + failover actions for multi-region routing. Goal is to reduce unsafe mass-evictions, preserve high-value tenant traffic, and enable graceful model downgrades (variant routing / quantized fallback / regional warm-standbys) when error budgets breach. This ticket covers SLI formulas, burn-rate thresholds, circuit-breaker states and transitions, routing actions, observability signals, ownership, and an implementation rollout plan for runtime + Console configuration.
sli_definitions: 1) Availability SLI: fraction of successful generation responses within 5s (status in 2xx and model generated tokens > 0). Measurement window: 5m sliding, aggregated to 1h for SLO evaluation. 2) Latency SLI: p95 and p99 end-to-end generation latency (client->response). Primary latency SLI used for SLO is p99. 3) Quality SLI: prompt-set pass-rate computed from periodic regression tests (per-endpoint canonical prompts). Quality SLI = fraction of prompts where model output score >= baseline threshold. 4) Error SLI: fraction of requests that incur server-side 5xx or model OOMs. 5) Tail-SLI: 95-99.9 quantile differential metric capturing tail amplification for long context requests.
normalization_and_budgeting: We will compute a normalized error-score per model-endpoint using quantile-based normalization: for each model variant, compute historical p99 latency and tail-sli (99.9). Convert to a percentile rank against peer models in the same family and scale to a 0-1 error propensity score. Combine quality SLI drop and latency tail score with configurable weights to produce a composite burn signal. Error budgets are allocated per-endpoint and then subdivided across model variants by 'priority weight' (see model tiers). High-tier (critical customer) routes get >50% of reserved error-budget slice. Budgets refresh daily; burn-rate is computed over 1h and 6h windows for circuit-breaker decisions.
circuit_breaker_policy: Three-state circuit breaker per endpoint-model-variant: CLOSED (normal), SOFT_OPEN (throttled fallback), HARD_OPEN (evicted). Triggers: a) SOFT_OPEN when 1h burn rate > 3x baseline OR p99 latency > configured threshold for 5 consecutive 1m windows. Action: route 30-70% traffic to fallback variant (configurable per route), reduce batch sizes for remaining traffic, emit 'soft-breaker' alert. b) HARD_OPEN when 6h sustained burn rate > 5x baseline OR error SLI > 10% sustained for 30m. Action: evict model variant from serving pool, immediate routing to warm-standby region or lower-cost variant; deprioritize KV cache writes for that route for 10m. Recovery: automated probation after 30m in HARD_OPEN where traffic ramped to 1% for smoke tests; requires green health metrics for 10m to transition to SOFT_OPEN and then CLOSED.
failover_and_routing_actions: Priority-first routing: each endpoint has a prioritized fallback chain (primary variant -> quantized variant -> lexicographic cheaper model -> regional warm-standby -> degrade-with-structured-response). On SOFT_OPEN, traffic is split proportionally by priority weights; on HARD_OPEN, traffic is rehomed to next available slot. Warm-standby regions keep a small reserve of model warm sessions (configurable) and are pre-authorized for fast promotion. All fallback responses must include the X-Redwood-Fallback header with reason code and variant id. For stateful features (KV cache), we use 'cache-specified fallthrough' to avoid cache poisoning. For private deployments, policy defaults to deny cross-region reroute unless tenant permits inter-region failover in their config.
observability_and_alerting: Signals to surface: continuous error-budget burn-rate (1h/6h), p99/p999 latency trend, model-specific 5xx rate, quality-regression failures (per-prompt), traffic-shift anomalies. Alerts: P0 Pager when HARD_OPEN for >10m affecting >5% of org traffic; P1 Slack for SOFT_OPEN; automated ticket creation for HARD_OPEN events with attached playback logs and sample requests. Console additions: per-endpoint 'budget meter' with predicted exhaustion timeline, per-variant contribution waterfall, and 'what-if' simulation slider for split percentages.
runbook_summary: Immediate steps when circuit-breaker fires: 1) Triage: identify variant and scope (region/tenant). 2) Mitigation: apply configured split to fallback variant, reduce concurrency and batch sizes for impacted variant. 3) Stabilize: if HARD_OPEN, fully evict and promote warm-standby; run regression prompts. 4) Postmortem: capture root cause, model-behavior trace (token-level), and adjust weights/thresholds. Runbook links will be added to Console and on-call rotation notes.
implementation_tasks: Runtime: add per-variant circuit-breaker state machine and split routing support (ENG)
Runtime: implement quantile-based normalization pipeline and store normalized scores in model meta-index (ENG)
Console: UI for editing fallback chains and viewing budget meters (PX/Frontend)
Observability: dashboards and alerts for burn-rate windows and tail-SLI (SRE)
Evals: assemble per-endpoint canonical prompt-sets and pass thresholds (Applied ML)
Docs: PRD and runbook for on-call and SE teams (PM/Docs)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary 2 endpoints): implement normalization + soft-open only, run for 2 weeks with 'simulation mode' where routing decisions are logged but not enforced. Phase 2 (partial rollout 10% of endpoints): enable SOFT_OPEN enforcement and enable Console controls for split percentages. Phase 3 (global): enable HARD_OPEN with auto-eviction and warm-standby promotion. Each phase gated by SLO-preservation metrics and a safety checklist (no regressions in quality SLI and <2x error spikes during transition).
open_questions: What default weights should apply to latency tail vs quality in composite score? (proposal: 0.6 latency_tail, 0.4 quality)
Should private deployments default to deny cross-region failover? (proposal: yes, unless tenant opts in)
How to expose per-tenant priority weights in Console without overwhelming UI? (proposal: tenant presets)
What is the acceptable minimum warm-standby session count per model family to keep promotion latency < 500ms?
